slot.brief: Effect of adding a constant (or scaling) on mean and variance of a data set; ask the new mean and SD.

stem: A data set has mean $4$ and standard deviation $2$. If each observation $x$ is replaced by $3x+1$, the new mean and standard deviation are
working:
$\mu_{3x+1}=3\mu_x+1=3(4)+1=13$\n$\sigma_{3x+1}=|3|\sigma_x=3(2)=6$

Independent check: New mean = 3(4)+1 = 13; new standard deviation = |3|(2) = 6.
solution: For a linear transformation $y=ax+b$, the mean becomes $a\mu+b$ and the standard deviation becomes $|a|\sigma$. Thus, $$\mu_y=3(4)+1=13,\qquad \sigma_y=|3|(2)=6.$$
